author: GamingBolt
description:
The 1999 tactical RPG returns in the modern remake of Front Mission 3. This actually isn’t the first release of the remake, however, since a Switch version came out in 2025. This console version fixes some of the issues of the Switch version in key areas. The most notable enhancement from the original 1999 game is in the audio/visual department. 

Backgrounds are rendered in 3D from the old pixelated 2D style. The result is much better lighting and greater contrasts between colors. Though, some details are missing and fans are divided about the overall translation. 

The combat is pretty much unchanged from the Switch version, though it’s much smoother than the PS1 original. Some quality of life improvements are still missing, however, which slows down the tactical gameplay. 

Front Mission 3 Remake releases for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S, so suit up your mecha and get ready for some old school tactical action.
title: Front Mission 3 Remake PS5 Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
Yakuza 3 has long occupied an awkward place in the series’ history. It was the franchise’s first major leap onto new hardware at the time, and while it introduced fan-favorite characters and locations, it also carried design decisions that haven’t aged particularly well. 

Slow, defensive combat and uneven pacing caused both newcomers and longtime fans to bounce off the experience, even after the 2019 remaster, which didn’t really smooth those problems away. 

The remake, donning the Kiwami badge, aims to solve the remasters’ problems by restructuring parts of the story and touching up the gameplay with added and refined elements. Whether you’re into the day-in-the-life dad sim angle or just want to smash some gang members in the face using the new combat style, Yakuza Kiwami 3 looks to be a remake worth diving into.
title: Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties - 15 Features You NEED TO KNOW Before You Purchase

author: GamingBolt
description:
With less than a week remaining before Code Vein 2 attempts to give a flying start to Bandai Namco's tryst with 2026, we think that it's a good time to talk about why the sequel has us excited to dive back into a universe with some very interesting twists. 

The Revenant Hunter could just be a protagonist whose adventure is every bit as great as the first game while managing to build on everything that made it stand out in the past. 

Of course, there are a few changes that we see as risky moves, but given the new additions that accompany them, things could turn out quite well for the second instalment in a franchise that boasts of such an interesting concept and a penchant for storytelling that was quite riveting to begin with. 

Join us as we take you through why this one has us hyped, and you might perhaps find the next big game to satisfy your itch for some action and a great adventure to lose yourself in.
title: You Are ABSOLUTELY Not Ready For Code Vein 2
